checks.command: git diff --check on four assigned files

findings.scenario: After the cache reaches ready, each scheduled sync immediately clears ready and holds busy until node checks finish. A data GET during every otherwise healthy periodic refresh returns 503, exposing ordinary RPC latency as browsing failures. Existing HTTP test double keeps readiness true during sync and misses this interaction.
findings.repair: Have validated data GETs await the already active sync promise before checking readiness/querying. Keep status immediate. Do not start an extra sync, retry, or serve an unauthenticated/stale projection; failed or incomplete sync must still return 503. Test a ready index entering delayed routine sync, concurrent GETs sharing that one sync and its successful/failing outcomes.

review: Read all four source/test files before verdict. Actual SDK block bodies explicitly include transactions; decoder binds transaction effects to canonical blocks and exact reviewed class/emitter/schema.

Cold cache ranges are completely re-fetched and re-decoded before ready. Equality rejects omitted/injected cached events even with retained block hashes. Matching cache JSON/checkpoints are not themselves authority.

Range/event/record/snapshot bounds, CAS-before-publish, bounded rollback, detached metadata and strict GET-only public routes are retained. No private/wallet routes or raw upstream errors are exposed.
Scope is immutable; deployment anchor is copied; source tests use labelled SDK-data doubles and real processed ABI/SQLite.
limitations: No live-chain index qualification or browser-to-canonical-index journey was run by this reviewer.

The timeout races bound caller waiting, not cancellation of arbitrary injected node/storage implementations. CLI transport independently aborts at 20 seconds; do not describe generic injected adapters as hard-cancelled.
Capacity bounds are explicit implementation limits; full product scale/privacy/release acceptance remains open.
